conventions.convention: Complex L-infinity consists of Borel functions modulo globally Haar-null sets, with the essential-supremum norm. Locally null sets are not identified with zero.
Left translation is L_g f(x)=f(g⁻¹x). A mean is positive, complex-linear and unital; left invariance tests every group element and every L-infinity class.
Reiter densities are nonnegative L1 classes of norm one. Compact-test defects include zero in the supremum, so the empty-test defect is zero; nets converge uniformly on every compact test set.
Følner witnesses are Borel sets of positive finite left Haar measure. Only left translates occur, and the empty compact test has defect zero.
UCB consists of actual bounded functions whose left-translation orbit is sup-norm continuous. Its class map into global L-infinity is isometric.
Almost invariance uses strict pointwise displacement inequalities and unit vectors, testing every compact set and every positive tolerance. The zero representation has no almost invariant vectors.

Kazhdan thresholds are extended-real suprema with zero adjoined. Empty-test displacement is zero and the zero-space representation has displacement constant +∞. Compact test sets include the threshold endpoint; no such endpoint equivalence is asserted for noncompact tests.

Spectral gap means that the trivial representation is not weakly contained in the restriction to the orthogonal complement of the fixed subspace. The displacement reformulation is stated only under LCH and AC hypotheses.
Relative property (T) and relative Kazhdan pairs are defined for arbitrary subgroups. The distance estimates separately require a closed normal subgroup.
The semidirect product uses coordinates (k,v) and multiplication (k,v)(k′,v′)=(kk′,v+kv′). The dual action on frequencies is ξ↦(k⁻¹)ᵀξ.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. A locally compact Hausdorff group is amenable if and only if it satisfies Reiter's condition (P1), for a fixed left Haar measure; the equivalence is independent of Haar normalization.

Assume AC. For a topological group, property (T), existence of a compact Kazhdan pair, and positivity of the Kazhdan threshold on some compact set are equivalent. For any Kazhdan pair (Q,ε), a (Q,δε)-invariant vector with 0<δ≤1 has distance at most δ times its norm from the fixed subspace.

Assume AC. For an LCH group with fixed left Haar measure, f∈L1 and φ∈L-infinity, f*φ(x)=∫f(y)φ(y⁻¹x)dμ(y) defines a representative-independent actual UCB function, bounded by ||f||1||φ||∞. It satisfies left equivariance, the stated translation-defect bound, bilinearity, and (f*b)*φ=f*(b*φ) for f,b∈L1.

Assume AC. A topological invariant mean on L-infinity of an LCH group with fixed left Haar measure yields a net g_j of probability densities with ||f*g_j−g_j||1→0 for every probability density f, uniformly on norm-compact subsets of the probability densities.

Assume AC. For an LCH group with fixed left Haar measure, amenability is equivalent to 1_G≺λ_G, equivalently to almost invariant unit vectors in the left regular representation on every compact test set.

Assume AC. An LCH group with fixed left Haar measure is amenable if and only if, for every compact Q and ε>0, there is a Borel F of positive finite measure with Δ_Q(F)≤ε; equivalently, it admits a left Følner net.

Assume AC. For every complex C*-algebra A, without unit or separability hypotheses, and every nonzero x∈A, some nonzero irreducible nondegenerate star-representation σ satisfies σ(x)≠0. Consequently the intersection of all such kernels is zero, including the stated zero-algebra convention.

Assume AC. For G=SL2(R)⋉R² and its translation subgroup N, the four-element set consisting of the two displayed elementary unipotents and their inverses admits ε0∈(0,1] such that every representation with a (Q0,ε0)-invariant unit vector has a nonzero N-invariant vector. In particular (G,N) has relative property (T).

Assume AC. For a topological group, closed normal N and relative Kazhdan pair (Q,ε), dist(ξ,H^N)≤ε⁻¹Δ_Q(ξ) and sup over n∈N of ||π(n)ξ−ξ||≤2ε⁻¹Δ_Q(ξ). Moreover relative property (T) gives a uniform positive displacement bound on every compact Q whose positive powers cover G, for representations without nonzero N-invariants.
For n≥2, every matrix in SLn(R) is a product of at most M(n)=2n²+6n elementary transvections E_ij(t); identity factors E_ij(0) are allowed.

Assume AC. For an LCH group with left Haar measure and its left regular representation, compactness, finite total Haar measure, existence of a nonzero regular invariant vector, and membership of the constant function 1 in L2 are equivalent. Total Haar measure is always positive.

seams_checked.note: The page, prop-sl2-r-does-not-have-property-t and cex-sl2-r-complementary-series-destroys-property-t faithfully use the spherical range 0<ν<1, positive weighted even K-lines, irreducibility and compact-uniform coefficient convergence as ν↑1.
